title: Compact audit ledger with geo-residency tags and WORM-backed tamper-proof exporter
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: Customers in regulated regions require compact, queryable audit evidence for admin actions, access events, and configuration changes that is provably tamper-proof, tied to data residency policies, and automatically exported for legal/forensic review. Current audit capture is verbose, region-agnostic, and lacks a reliable sealed export that meets WORM/retention proof expectations.

Goal: Produce a compact audit ledger format that summarizes per-event minimal metadata (actor, action-type, object, timestamp, residency tag, retention-hint, change-hash) and a signing/envelope workflow that writes periodic sealed snapshots into region-bound WORM storage with rotation manifests and verifiable integrity proofs. The exporter must support retention enforcement, automatic evidence packages for subpoenas/legal hold, and a reporting endpoint for compliance teams.

Scope:
- Capture admin actions, access grants/revocations, role/permission config changes, and service-account operations.
- Attach a geo-residency tag derived from the request routing policy and resource residency mapping.
- Create compact snapshot batches (hourly by default) that include a Merkle root, signed index, and manifest.
- Push sealed snapshots to region-specific WORM buckets (S3 Object Lock or equivalent) with retention metadata and an audit manifest stored separately in a slow, immutable index.
- Provide automated evidence package generation (zip + provenance.json) for retention/forensic requests.

Out of scope for this ticket: full-text event retention for high-volume debug traces, UI for console browsing (will add follow-up PM ticket), cross-region replication strategy (handled by separate infra work).

Constraints & compliance requirements:
- Retention TTLs must be honored per-customer policy; WORM buckets enforced with legal-hold override path only available to compliance service with multi-sig approval.
- Signed artifacts must be verifiable by external auditors (PKI key rotation plan required).
- Residency tags must align with customer's placement and not be inferred solely from IP.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Compact ledger vs full event store: compact ledger reduces cost and is sufficient for legal evidence but will not replace detailed trace stores for debugging.
- Use S3 Object Lock (WORM) vs HSM-attested archival: start with cloud-native WORM for speed to market, design interfaces to swap in on-prem HSM escrow later.
- Hourly vs daily snapshots: hourly chosen to balance size and time-to-evidence; configurable per-org.

Success criteria:
- Sealed snapshots are produced on schedule and land in region-bound WORM buckets with retention metadata.
- Evidence packages can be generated on-demand within SLA (<=24h for standard requests) and include integrity proofs that verify against a published public key.
- Residency tag correctness >99.9% for test dataset.
- End-to-end e2e tests + signature verification in CI.
acceptance_criteria: Hourly compact snapshots containing batched events (min metadata) are produced and contain a Merkle root and signed index.
Snapshots are written to region-specific WORM storage with Object Lock enabled and retention metadata set according to customer policy.
Automated evidence exporter can assemble a per-customer package with manifest.json, signature, and a human-readable summary within 24 hours.
End-to-end verification: given a snapshot and public key, an auditor can verify the Merkle root and signature via CLI documented in the runbook.
Retention enforcement: attempts to delete sealed snapshots are rejected by policy and alerts are generated to Security if a legal-hold override is attempted.
Console/ops dashboard displays export status and per-region counts (backfilled for last 90 days) for operational visibility.
implementation_notes: Capture layer: extend existing audit emitter to tag events with residency_id and retention_hint; add compact serializer to map to ledger rows.
Batching: implement compact-batcher service (serverless or k8s job) that periodically computes Merkle tree and signs index with compliance key (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8179).
Exporter: S3 uploader with Object Lock config and lifecycle tags; use kms key per-region and record key-id in manifest (PR: github.com/redwood/storage/pull/2321).

Index: append to an immutable index store (read-only for auditors) with per-snapshot metadata for fast lookup and report generation (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Compact+Audit+Ledger).
Evidence package: cli/tooling to assemble zip that contains snapshots, manifest, signing-cert, and a short narrative with queryable ids for legal teams.
PKI: coordinate with Security for key generation, rotation cadence, and verification tooling (ticketed with SecOps).
CI: add signature verification step and a small e2e generator test that simulates cross-region event flow.
